correctness.rationale: The binomial decomposition for unanimous and split triads is exact. Centering gives T(x,y)=(-P_A(y),-P_B(x)), where P_i(z)=a_i z-b_i z^3. The parameter restrictions imply b_i>0 and 0<=P_i'(1)=3(u_i-v_i), so each P_i strictly increases and is strictly concave on (0,1). T squared is the product of two odd increasing strictly concave scalar compositions with common derivative Theta at zero, so each has only zero fixed when Theta<=1 and exactly one stable positive and one stable negative nonzero fixed when Theta>1. This classifies all T-periodic points because monotone scalar functions have no nontrivial cycles. The exact cubic expansion at Theta=1 gives strictly positive coefficients K_A,K_B and n^(-1/2) decay; no finite calculation substitutes for the global proof. Exact-rational verifier executes correctly for the normal form and representative parameters. The finite-population process is excluded.

value.rationale: The source leaves cross-population organization outside its one-population majority analysis, while older community models treat no contrarian composition dependence. Socially motivated split response propensities and reciprocal cross-group sampling generate an interpretable competition between static antagonistic majorities and synchronous reversals; both may be locally attracting at the SAME parameters. The product criterion exactly decides global balancing vs three attractor coexistence over a nontrivial four-parameter domain, with complete attraction basins and critical exponent. It is more than a diagonal parameter substitution or a tabulated example; it classifies the full four-dimensional response range meeting natural monotonicity/concavity hypotheses. No statement is made for finite populations or outside the regime.
